title: 10 best LinkedPhone alternatives to try in 2026
summary: Worried LinkedPhone isn’t a fit for your business? Here are 10 of the best LinkedPhone alternatives, plus prices, features, and limitations.
body_markdown:
It’s hard to look past a[business phone number app](https://www.quo.com/blog/best-business-phone-number-apps/) like LinkedPhone: it’s transparent, simple, and easy to use. But look a little closer, and you’ll start to realize that you get what you pay for. It sacrifices valuable features that can save your team time to keep the price down.


This guide covers 10 LinkedPhone alternatives — including their prices, features, and limitations — so you can find a better fit for your growing business. It also explains where LinkedPhone falls short and why businesses move to LinkedPhone competitors.


##


**Comparing the best LinkedPhone alternatives**


How do the best LinkedPhone alternatives stack up?


See for yourself in this comparison table:


Provider Starting price Unlimited calling to US & Canada SMS/MMS to US & Canada Shared phone numbers Additional phone numbers


LinkedPhone $19.99 per user per month For US and Canadian customers only For US and Canadian customers only ✔️ $5 per number per month


Quo, formerly OpenPhone $15 per user per month ✔️ ✔️ ✔️ $5 per number per month


Nextiva $15 per user per month ✔️ 100 SMS per user per month Shared texting requires upgrade Undisclosed fee


Dialpad $15 per user per month ✔️ For US and Canadian customers only ✔️ Requires upgrade


Ooma $19.95 per user per month ✔️ Requires upgrade ✔️ $9.95 per number per month


GoTo Connect Contact for a quote ✔️ limited toll-free minutes Credits differ per region Requires upgrade Contact for a quote


Vonage $13.99 per user per month for 1-4 users ✔️ Local US and Canadian numbers only Shared line appearances only Starts at $4.99 per number per month


RingCentral $20 per user per month ✔️ 25 messages per user per month ✔️ calls only $4.99 per number per month


8×8 Contact for a quote ✔️ ✔️ ✔️ Contact for a quote


Aircall $30 per user per month ✔️ ✔️ ✔️ $6 per number per month


Grasshopper $14 per month ✔️ MMS messaging for local numbers only Requires upgrade $9 per number per month


Let’s take a closer look at all 10 options.


### **1. Quo: Best LinkedPhone alternative for small and growing businesses**


#### Pros


- Shared phone numbers on every plan
- 9,000+ integrations on all plans via Zapier and Make
- Competitive international calls and texts
- AI agent, Sona
- Internal threads, or team chat


#### Cons


- No verification through two-factor authentication*


**Nearly all virtual phone numbers share this problem. Companies like Facebook, Uber, and Google rarely let you authenticate accounts through a virtual phone number.*


Quo is a VoIP provider for startups, scaleups, and growing small businesses. In addition to free calls and texts to anyone in the US and Canada, you get one local, toll-free, or vanity number per member on your account. Additional numbers only cost $5 extra per month.


With Quo, you can turn any number into a[shared phone number](https://www.quo.com/blog/how-to-share-a-business-phone-number-with-your-team/) , which lets multiple team members call and text from the same number. You can also make international calls on all plans.


Need to keep everyone on the same page? Quo has[internal threads](https://support.quo.com/core-concepts/team-collaboration/internal-threads) where team members can leave comments on conversations and tag each other to delegate tasks. You can also tap into Quo’s[call views](https://support.quo.com/core-concepts/inboxes/call-views) to find calls that haven’t yet received a response or seamlessly take over follow-ups for other team members.


You can use Quo’s AI[call tags](https://www.quo.com/product/ai/call-tagging) to automatically tag calls after they end, with labels like “Billing issue” or “Positive conversation.” This makes it easier to keep your inbox organized and helps team members find customer conversations faster.


Want to use an AI agent that can handle customer calls?[Sona](https://www.quo.com/sona) , Quo’s AI agent, answers incoming calls and takes messages, responds to frequently asked questions, and can record important details you’ll need to follow up with the caller when you’re available.


Quo can also help you put text messaging on autopilot. We offer texting automations that many[Quo alternatives](https://www.quo.com/blog/quo-alternatives/) don’t, such as:


- [Scheduled messages](https://www.quo.com/blog/how-to-schedule-texts/) that ensure you only send texts during business hours in your customer’s time zone
- Saved replies and templated texts (aka[snippets](https://support.quo.com/core-concepts/messaging/snippets) ) to respond faster to customers when they ask common questions
- [Auto-replies](https://www.quo.com/blog/texting-auto-reply-examples/) that instantly respond to missed calls, texts, and voicemails so your customer gets a response when you’re not available to pick up the phone


And like LinkedPhone, Quo integrates with Zapier. You can also connect with Slack, Zapier, and Make, as well as CRMs like[HubSpot](https://www.quo.com/integrations/hubspot) and[Salesforce](https://www.quo.com/integrations/salesforce) , so you can keep your tech stack connected. You can also easily surface insights and save time following up using Quo’s Claude and ChatGPT connectors.


See why 90,000+ businesses trust Quo by[signing up for a seven-day free trial](https://my.quo.com/signup) .


#### **Key features of Quo**


- AI call tags
- Call views
- [Call screening](https://www.quo.com/product/call-management/call-screening)
- Texting automations like scheduled messages, snippets, and auto-replies
- Automations with Zapier and Make
- [Quo API](https://www.quo.com/api)
- Shared phone numbers
- [Call recording](https://www.quo.com/product/call-recording)
- HIPAA compliant, with a Business Associate Agreement


#### **Quo pricing**


[Quo’s pricing](https://www.quo.com/blog/quo-pricing/) makes it easy to scale your business with plans that grow alongside you:


- **Starter** : $15 per user per month for free calling and texting to US and Canadian numbers, shared phone numbers, snippets, scheduled messages, auto-replies, basic call forwarding, integrations with email, Slack, and Zapier, email ticket support, and more
- **Business** : $23 per user per month for CRM integrations (HubSpot and Salesforce), advanced[call forwarding](https://www.quo.com/product/call-forwarding) options,[automatic call recording](https://www.quo.com/product/call-recording/automatic-call-recording) ,[AI call summaries](https://www.quo.com/features/call-summary) ,[phone menus](https://www.quo.com/blog/phone-menu/) , custom[ring orders](https://support.quo.com/core-concepts/administration/call-flows/ring-groups) , analytics, access to live chat support, and more
- **Scale** : $35 per user per month for AI call tags, dedicated onboarding support, priority access to chat and email support, and conditional call routing


### **2. Nextiva: Best for teams that use Microsoft products**


#### Pros


- Native integrations with Microsoft tools
- Omnichannel communication with calls, texts, social media, live chat, and video


#### Cons


- Limited texting on the base plan
- Toll-free number requires an upgrade
- Call recording requires an add-on or upgrade


Nextiva is a communications platform built for omnichannel teams. It combines calls, texts, and social media channels into a single workspace. Nextiva also integrates seamlessly with Microsoft products like Teams and Dynamics, making it a good fit for businesses that are already in the Microsoft ecosystem.


Unlike LinkedPhone, Nextiva has limited calling and texting features on its base Small Business plan, with advanced features blocked by a paywall:


- Nextiva limits texting on the Core plan to 100 messages per user per month. Unlimited messages require upgrading to the Scale plan, which starts at $75 per user per month.
- Toll-free numbers are available on the Core plan as an add-on, or you can upgrade to the Engage plan.
- If you want to integrate Nextiva with Microsoft Teams, you’ll need to purchase an add-on if you’re on the Core plan or upgrade to the Engage plan.
- CRM integrations are an additional paid add-on regardless of which plan you choose.


The cherry on top? Nextiva doesn’t offer a free trial, meaning you can’t test the platform before committing to a paid plan.


If you need an all-in-one communications system that connects phones, chat, social, and Microsoft products, Nextiva might be a strong contender. Just be prepared for upgrades (and the price tag that comes with them). If the pricing isn’t for you, consider a[Nextiva alternative](https://www.quo.com/blog/nextiva-alternatives/) .


#### Key features of Nextiva


**


- Integrations with messaging apps like WhatsApp, Facebook, and Instagram
- Digital fax requires an upgrade
- Voice and video call recording require upgrades
- Microsoft integrations requires upgrades
- Business calls and texts requires an upgrade


#### Nextiva pricing


**


There are three[Nextiva pricing](https://www.quo.com/blog/nextiva-pricing/) plans for small businesses:


- **Core:** $15 per user per month for business calls and texts, social media messaging, video calls, and access to a mobile app
- **Engage:** $25 per user per month for access to toll-free numbers, online fax, call recording, live chat, and the ability for customers to send your team SMS messages
- **Scale:** $75 per user per month for call transcriptions and summaries, IVR, and unlimited text messages


### **3. Dialpad: Best for contact centers**


#### Pros


- Numbers available in 50+ countries, with an upgrade
- Unlimited domestic calling and texting


#### Cons


- Additional numbers require an upgrade
- No international texting on the base plan
- Extensions are locked behind the highest tier


Dialpad is a[cloud communications](https://www.quo.com/blog/cloud-communications/) platform that supports local numbers in 50+ countries. It also integrates with CRMs like Salesforce, Zendesk, and HubSpot. Plus, it offers unlimited office locations, which are ideal for large contact centers with multiple physical branches that want to organize team members by location.


But scaling with Dialpad isn’t always easy. Like LinkedPhone, Dialpad requires upgrades to purchase essential features like extra numbers, extensions, and international texting. This can be frustrating for fast-growing teams that don’t want to pay for a full plan upgrade.


Dialpad still stands apart from LinkedPhone by offering stronger[CRM integrations](https://www.quo.com/blog/crm-phone-integration/) and better international coverage. But if you’re looking for a solution that can scale more easily as you grow, it might be worth exploring[Dialpad alternatives](https://www.quo.com/blog/dialpad-alternatives/) .


#### Key features of Dialpad


**


- Business SMS; international SMS requires an upgrade
- [Phone number extensions](https://www.quo.com/blog/phone-extension/) require upgrades
- International numbers require an upgrade
- Integrations on the base plan
- Desktop and mobile apps


#### Dialpad pricing


**


There are three[Dialpad pricing](https://www.quo.com/blog/dialpad-pricing/) plans for you to choose from:


- **Standard:** $15 per user per month for one user for calling, texting, team messaging, voicemail transcriptions, and access to Google Workspace and Microsoft 365 integrations
- **Pro:** $25 per user per month for CRM integrations, 10 office locations, and local number support in 50+ countries, with a three-user minimum
- **Enterprise:** Custom quote for unlimited[ring groups](https://www.quo.com/features/ring-groups) , dial by extension, and unlimited office locations, with a 100-user minimum


### **4. Ooma: Best VoIP for unlimited calling in Mexico and Puerto Rico**


#### Pros


- Unlimited calling in the US, Canada, Mexico, and Puerto Rico
- Texting in the US and Canada


#### Cons


- Call recording requires an upgrade
- Texting isn’t available on the base plan
- Voicemail transcriptions require an upgrade


[Ooma](https://www.quo.com/blog/ooma-pricing/) is a Canadian phone provider that serves homes and small businesses. It’s available in the US and Canada and includes unlimited calls to Mexico and Puerto Rico.


The base plan provides basic capabilities like a mobile app, virtual receptionist, and call forwarding.


But Ooma’s lower-tier Ooma Office Essentials plan is very limited. You can’t text at all unless you upgrade to Ooma Office Pro, and you’re limited to only 100 messages per user per month. You can’t use the desktop app, access voicemail transcriptions, or record any calls, either.


If you need integrations, you’ll have to sign up for at least Ooma Office Pro Plus. And right now, the Microsoft Teams integration is only available on the Enterprise plan.


#### Key features of Ooma


**


- Unlimited calling in the US, Canada, Mexico, and Puerto Rico
- 911 service
- Hold music
- Call transfer
- Virtual receptionist


#### Ooma pricing


**


Ooma has four[pricing plans](https://www.quo.com/blog/ooma-pricing/) to consider:


- **Ooma Office Essentials:** $19.95 per user per month for unlimited calling in the US, Canada, Mexico, and Puerto Rico and a virtual receptionist and a virtual fax
- **Ooma Office Pro:** $24.95 per user per month for 100 text messages, calling from the desktop app, and call analytics
- **Ooma Office Pro Plus:** $29.95 per user per month for 400 text messages, AI transcription, CRM integration, team chat, and third-party integrations
- **Ooma Office Enterprise:** Custom price for access to Microsoft Teams integration, advanced analytics and CX features, and custom implementation


### **5. GoTo Connect: Best for making calls to international customers**


#### Pros


- Free calls to 50+ countries
- Shared inbox requires an upgrade


#### Cons


- No transparent pricing
- Limited toll-free minutes
- Texting is only available in the US, Canada, the UK, and Australia


[GoTo Connect](https://www.quo.com/blog/goto-connect-alternatives/) is a business communication solution with tools for texting, calling, and video meetings. Its base plan lets you make calls to 50+ countries and includes call handling features like call recording.


But GoTo Connect falls short when it comes to transparency and scalability. Pricing isn’t listed publicly, so you’ll have to contact sales for a quote. You’ll also need to upgrade if you want shared inboxes for better team collaboration, which makes managing calls and messages tougher on lower-tier plans.


You should also keep an eye on toll-free limits: each plan has a max of 1,000 toll-free minutes shared across everyone on your account. Once you go over the limit, you’ll pay $0.019 per minute extra, which can get expensive fast if you handle hundreds of calls per month.


Planning to send texts? GoTo Connect only supports messaging to US, UK, Canadian, and Australian numbers. And toll-free numbers can’t send or receive texts at all.


If you need international calling and don’t mind contacting sales, GoTo Connect can be a viable LinkedPhone alternative. Just get ready for built-in restrictions around texting, calling, and scaling your plan.


#### Key features of GoTo Connect


**


- Unlimited free calls in 50+ countries
- Paging and intercom
- Hot desking
- Call routing
- Ring groups


#### GoTo Connect pricing


**


[GoTo Connect’s pricing](https://www.quo.com/blog/goto-connect-pricing/) plans aren’t publicly available. That said, you can still see its plans and features listed on the website:


- **Phone System:** Free calls in 50+ countries, team chat, auto-attendants, a mobile app, video meetings, and the Microsoft Teams integration
- **Customer Experience (CX):** AI call summaries, Zendesk integration, and shared inboxes
- **CX Complete:** Intelligent call routing, auto queue callback, auto dialer, and custom ringbacks
- **Contact Center:** AI chat analysis, agent monitoring, skills assignment, and ring strategy options


### **6. Vonage: Best for video conferencing**


#### Pros


- 200-participant video meetings with an upgrade
- Customizable APIs


#### Cons


- Best features require an upgrade
- Integrations require the premium plan
- Expensive compared to other providers


[Vonage](https://www.quo.com/blog/vonage-alternatives/) is a cloud communications platform that works across desktop, mobile, and browser apps. Its base plan covers essentials like voicemail, text messaging, and phone number porting, as well as video conferences on higher tiers.


Vonage and LinkedPhone have several similarities, like supporting calls on traditional office desk phones. But with Vonage, you’ll need to upgrade to the Premium plan if you want to use desk phones, which costs $29.99 per user per month.


You’ll also notice that the bulk of Vonage’s features are locked behind more expensive plans. For example:


- Call groups are only available on the Advanced plan
- Team messaging is only available on the Premium plan
- Third-party integrations require the Premium plan, but you’ll only have access to 20+ apps


If you don’t want to upgrade for basic features, you may want to consider Vonage alternatives.


#### Key features of Vonage


**


- Video conferencing requires an upgrade
- Unlimited domestic calling
- [SMS and MMS](https://www.quo.com/blog/sms-vs-mms/) support
- Call groups requires an upgrade
- Voicemail; visual voicemail requires an upgrade
- Call recording requires an upgrade


#### Vonage pricing


**


[Vonage pricing](https://www.quo.com/blog/dialpad-pricing/) depends on how many users your business needs. Here’s how much each plan costs for teams of one to four users:


- **Mobile:** $13.99 per user per month for business texting, basic voicemail, and access to the desktop and mobile apps
- **Premium:** $20.99 per user per month for access to integrations, support for VoIP desk phones, unlimited video meetings, and team messaging
- **Advanced:** $27.99 per user per month for call groups, visual voicemail, and 15 hours of[on-demand call recording](https://www.quo.com/product/call-recording/on-demand-call-recording)


### **7. RingCentral: Best alternative for desk phone rentals**


#### Pros


- Traditional office phone rentals
- Advanced call monitoring is available


#### Cons


- Limited toll-free minutes and text messages
- “Unlimited” storage is subject to time-based deletion policies
- Phone rentals require a multi-year contract


[RingCentral](https://www.quo.com/blog/ringcentral-alternatives/) is one of the oldest cloud-based phone systems on this list and is well-known for supporting traditional landline setups. You can buy desk phones directly from their store or rent them through a multi-year contract.


RingCentral offers a similar range of features to LinkedPhone, like caller ID, voicemail transcriptions, and shared phone numbers. But unlike LinkedPhone, you’ll have access to video conferencing and[call management](https://www.quo.com/product/call-management) tools like call barging and whispering.


Unfortunately, RingCentral’s unified communications features come with limitations that require you to upgrade:


- The base plan only comes with 25 text messages per user per month, and the Advanced plan only bumps that up to 100.
- If you want to store more than 100,000 call recordings, you’ll need to upgrade to the Ultra plan. Plus, you’ll never be able to store call recordings for longer than 90 days unless you integrate with Dropbox or Google Drive.
- The base plan only includes 100 toll-free minutes per month, which likely won’t be enough if you get a lot of inbound calls.


And don’t forget RingCentral’s expensive fees — like its $30 price tag to purchase a[vanity number](https://www.quo.com/vanity-number) , plus a $4.99 setup fee.


#### Key features of RingCentral


**


- Unlimited domestic calling
- Deskphone rentals
- Shared voicemail
- Multi-level auto-attendants
- Call recording, automatic requires upgrade


#### RingCentral pricing


**


You can pick from among three[RingCentral pricing](https://www.quo.com/blog/ringcentral-pricing/) plans:


- **Core** : $20 per user per month for unlimited calls, 100 pooled toll-free minutes, and 25 texts per user per month
- **Advanced:** $25 per user per month for 1,000 pooled toll-free minutes, 100 texts per user per month, automatic call recording, and integrations with CRMs
- **Ultra:** $35 per user per month for 10,000 pooled toll-free minutes, 200 texts per user per month, and unlimited storage for files and call recordings


### **8. 8×8: Best LinkedPhone alternative for online payments**


#### Pros


- Secure payment processing
- International virtual phone numbers


#### Cons


- No transparent pricing
- Confusing features list
- Steep learning curve


8×8 is a business communications platform with plans for small businesses, contact centers, and enterprise teams. If its pre-built plans don’t suit your business, you can tap into its customizable communication APIs for voice, SMS, video, authentication, and omnichannel messaging.


Here’s a quick look at 8×8’s pre-built plans:


- 8×8’s Contact Center plan comes with self-service workflows and secure payment processing, which you can use to set up recurring online payments like rent or invoices.
- 8×8 Work lets you buy virtual phone numbers from around the world, including local, international, or toll-free numbers. However, toll-free numbers don’t support texting.
- 8×8’s Beyond the Contact Center lets you handle all customer messages from social media and messaging platforms in one place.


But according to past users, 8×8 has a history of overcomplicating things. There’s no public pricing available online, and its feature lists often overlap between plans. Reviewers also warn there’s a fairly steep learning curve for onboarding, setup, and navigation.


If your business needs to set up customer support self-service workflows or payment solutions for customers, 8×8 might be a good fit. But if you don’t want to spend the time or money to get everything running the way you want, you might consider some[8×8 alternatives](https://www.quo.com/blog/8x8-alternatives/) .


#### Key features of 8×8


**


- High-volume messaging
- Contact center analytics
- AI self-service workflows
- Secure payment processing
- Workforce engagement management


#### 8×8 pricing


**


[8×8’s pricing](https://www.quo.com/blog/8x8-pricing/) is no longer listed online. You have to contact the sales team to receive a custom quote.


### **9. Aircall: Best alternative for seamless integrations**


#### Pros


- 250+ integrations and API access available on the base plan
- Unlimited calling in the US and Canada


#### Cons


- User minimums on every plan
- AI call summaries require a paid add-on
- No text messages from toll-free numbers


[Aircall](https://www.quo.com/blog/aircall-alternatives/) is a customer communications platform with more than 250 integrations on the base plan. You can connect to CRMs like HubSpot and customer service platforms like Intercom and Zendesk without needing to upgrade.


There’s more to Aircall than just integrations, though — you get unlimited inbound and outbound calls to customers in the US and Canada. You’ll also have access to analytics data, call recording,[warm transfers](https://www.quo.com/blog/warm-transfer/) , and ring groups.


But what you *don’t* get with Aircall are AI tools like call summaries, which require the AI Assist add-on, priced at $9 per user per month. And keep in mind Aircall enforces user minimums, so the base plan will run you at least $90 per month for three users, even if you’re a two-person team.


#### Key features of Aircall


**


- 250+ integrations
- API access
- Ring groups
- AI call transcriptions via a paid add-on
- Warm transfers


#### Aircall pricing


**


There are three different[Aircall pricing](https://www.quo.com/blog/aircall-pricing/) plans:


- **Essentials:** $30 per user per month for 250+ integrations, access to the API, calling, and texting, with a three-user minimum
- **Professional:** $50 per user per month for integrations with Salesforce, unlimited call recording storage, and queue call back, with a three-user minimum
- **Custom:** Custom pricing for API developer support, custom onboarding, and unlimited calls worldwide, with a 25-user minimum


### **10. Grasshopper: Best LinkedPhone alternative with multi-digit phone extensions**


#### Pros


- Unlimited extensions, requires upgrading to the highest plan
- Local and toll-free phone numbers


#### Cons


- Only supports one user on the base plan
- Call recording requires an upgrade
- Limited third-party integrations


[Grasshopper](https://www.quo.com/blog/grasshopper-alternatives/) is a legacy VoIP provider that’s been around since 2003. It offers toll-free, local, and vanity numbers with multi-digit extensions, plus unlimited calling across the US and Canada.


Unlike most VoIP providers, Grasshopper’s pricing depends on how many phone numbers and extensions you want. Keep in mind new team members don’t automatically get their own numbers, so you’ll need to purchase additional numbers at $9 each. That’s nearly double what other providers charge.


Speaking of adding new members to your account, that’s not something you can do on Grasshopper’s base plan. You’ll also have to upgrade for simultaneous ring and call recording features. And no matter how much you upgrade, you won’t find shared phone numbers for texting or third-party integrations, aside from Skype and Google Voice.


#### Key features of Grasshopper


**


- Call forwarding
- Phone menus
- Business hours
- Simultaneous call handling requires an upgrade
- Extensions require an upgrade


#### Grasshopper pricing


**


As mentioned,[Grasshopper’s pricing](https://www.quo.com/blog/grasshopper-pricing/) depends on the phone numbers and extensions you want.


Here’s what that looks like on its three plans:


- **True Solo:** $14 per user per month for one user, one phone number, and one extension
- **Solo Plus:** $25 per user per month for unlimited users, one phone number, three extensions, call transfers, call recording, and simultaneous call handling
- **Small Business:** $55 per user per month for unlimited users, four phone numbers, and unlimited extensions


##


**Why businesses move to LinkedPhone alternatives**


LinkedPhone is a basic[VoIP](https://www.quo.com/blog/what-is-a-voip-phone/) system offering unlimited calls and texts to US and Canadian numbers. It offers basics you might expect from a virtual phone system, like[caller ID](https://www.quo.com/blog/business-caller-id/) . LinkedPhone also has a few advanced features, like skill-based[call routing](https://www.quo.com/product/call-routing) ,[business hours](https://www.quo.com/product/call-routing/business-hours-call-routing) , and a[phone menu](https://www.quo.com/blog/phone-menu/) .


They recently updated their pricing model, which is now based on how many phone numbers you order. Local and toll-free numbers cost $19.99 and $29.99 per month, respectively. Each number includes one user, and each additional user and phone number costs $5 per month. All features are available to all users, no matter how many phone numbers or seats you buy.


But while LinkedPhone advertises itself as a “small business solution,” it’s not really a fit for growing brands. Here are a few other key reasons why.


### **Texting registration isn’t as smooth as it should be**


Trying to register your number for business texting isn’t easy with LinkedPhone. Users have reported frustrating delays and poor communication during[The Campaign Registry](https://www.quo.com/blog/the-campaign-registry/) (TCR) process for[A2P 10DLC](https://www.quo.com/blog/what-is-a2p-10dlc/) .


For example, one[App Store](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/linked-phone-business-number/id1304985788) reviewer in March 2025 said LinkedPhone didn’t let them know there was an issue with their registration, and they couldn’t schedule clients for over a month:


Another user said their account was “under review” for weeks, and they still weren’t able to send texts at the time of writing the review, making it hard to keep their business running:


### **Third-party integrations are only available on Zapier**


LinkedPhone doesn’t list third-party integrations as a feature on their pricing page, nor are they listed anywhere else on the site. The only place LinkedPhone integrations are mentioned is on the Zapier website. If you don’t want to pay extra to use Zapier or if you prefer direct integrations, you’ll need to look at a LinkedPhone alternative.


### **Scaling your operations will be difficult**


LinkedPhone seems to be built more for solopreneurs. It lacks features growing businesses need, like native third-party integrations and a desktop app. They also claim to have no hidden fees, but they charge extra for premium AI features. There’s currently no information on their website about what counts as “premium.”


### **Inconsistent product ratings and reviews**


LinkedPhone’s product page says their app store rating is 4.7 stars, but on the Google Play Store, it’s 3.7 stars and 3.5 stars on G2. Compare this to Quo, which has consistently high scores across multiple sites/stores, including being the #1 rated in customer satisfaction on G2 and having more than 6,500 5-star reviews on the App Store.


### **LinkedPhone isn’t HIPAA compliant**


LinkedPhone notes on their website that they aren’t HIPAA compliant — not even as a paid upgrade. This immediately rules out LinkedPhone for certain industries.


### **You can’t make international calls**


LinkedPhone only supports calls to the US and Canada, which means you can’t make international calls. If your business needs to reach customers or team members overseas, you may need to use a secondary VoIP provider.


### **Customers report a lack of customer support**


Past LinkedPhone users say customer support isn’t responsive or quick to provide support on the phone. This might make it difficult to troubleshoot problems, as you can see in the review below on[Google Play](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.admin.linkedphone&gl=CA&hl=en) :

Quo’s plans are built to grow with you — no need to upgrade for more users, phone numbers, or base features. Whenever you’re ready, you can upgrade for automatic call recording, AI phone answering tools like Sona, and conditional call routing flows.
